en: 6. Saṅkhāra Yamaka 6.2 Pavattivāra 6.2.1.
Uppādavāra (The Chapter on Arising)
6.2.1.1 Present Chapter (Paccuppannavāra) 6.2.1.1.1 Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arises,
does verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arise for that person?
At the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation for those who are without applied thought and sustained thought, their bodily formation arises,
but their verbal formation does not arise. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those of the sense-sphere at the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation,
both their bodily formation and their verbal formation arise.
Or again, for whom verbal formation arises, for that person does bodily formation arise?
For those at the moment of the arising of applied and sustained thought (vitakka-vicāra) without inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation arises, but bodily formation does not arise.
[This is so] for those who have attained the first jhāna and for those sense-sphere beings (kāmāvacara) [at such a moment].
At the moment of arising, both verbal formation and bodily formation arise for those [beings].
For whom bodily formation arises, does mental formation also arise for them? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom mental formation arises, does bodily formation also arise for them?
At the moment of arising of consciousness when there is no inhalation or exhalation, the mental formation arises for them,
but the bodily formation does not arise for them. At the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation,
both the mental formation and the bodily formation arise for them.
For whom verbal formation arises, for that person does mental formation arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom mental formation arises, for that person does verbal formation arise?
At the moment of consciousness arising without applied thought (*vitakka*) and sustained thought (*vicāra*), mental formation arises for them, but verbal formation does not.
The verbal formation arises. At the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought, both the mental formation and the verbal formation arise for them.
6.2.1.1.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Where bodily formation arises, does verbal formation arise there?

In the second jhāna and the third jhāna, bodily formation arises there, but verbal formation does not arise there. In the first jhāna and in the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara), both bodily formation and verbal formation arise.
Or, where verbal formation arises, does bodily formation arise there?

In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, there arises there verbal formation, but bodily formation does not arise there. In the first jhāna of the sense-sphere, there arises there both verbal formation and bodily formation.
Where bodily formation arises, does mental formation arise there? Yes.
Or, where mental formation arises, does bodily formation arise there?
In the fourth jhāna, whether in the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) or the immaterial sphere (arūpāvacara),
mental formation arises there, but bodily formation does not arise there. In the first, second, and third jhānas, and in the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara),
both mental formation and bodily formation arise there.
Wherever verbal formation arises, there mental formation arises? Yes.
Or, wherever mental formation arises, there verbal formation arises?
In the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna, mental formation arises there, but verbal formation does not arise there.
Verbal formation arises. In the first jhāna—whether in the sense sphere, the fine-material sphere, or the immaterial sphere—therein both mental formation and verbal formation arise.
6.2.1.1.3. Positive Person-Space Analysis.
For whomsoever, wherever, the bodily formation arises … [etc.
… (The "for whom" and "wherever" sections are identical. 6.2.1.1.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom bodily formation does not arise, for that person does verbal formation not arise?

At the moment of the arising of applied and sustained thought (vitakka-vicāra) without inhalation and exhalation, bodily formation does not arise for them, but verbal formation does not fail to arise for them.
[This is so] for all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, provided there is no inhalation or exhalation.

At the moment of arising of a consciousness without applied thought and without sustained thought, and for those who have attained cessation and non-percipient beings, neither the bodily formation nor the verbal formation arises. Or, conversely,
for whomsoever the verbal formation does not arise, does the bodily formation not arise for them?

At the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation, when they are without applied thought and sustained thought, verbal formation does not arise for them, but bodily formation does not fail to arise for them. For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those with consciousness whose mind is without applied thought and sustained thought at the moment of its arising,
for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings, verbal formation [does not arise].
And the bodily formation does not arise, and the mental formation does not arise.
For whom the bodily formation does not arise, for that one does the mental formation not arise?
For those at the moment of consciousness-arising without inhalation and exhalation, the bodily formation does not arise, but for them [the mental formation does arise].

The mental formation does not arise. For all those at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings, neither the bodily formation nor the mental formation arises.
Or conversely, for whomsoever the mental formation does not arise, does the bodily formation not arise for them? Yes, it does.
For whom verbal formation does not arise, for them mental formation does not arise?
At the moment of consciousness arising without applied thought and sustained thought, for them verbal formation does not arise, but it is not the case that mental formation does not arise for them.
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings...
For them, neither verbal formation nor mental formation arises.
Or rather, for whom mental formation does not arise, does verbal formation not arise for that person? Yes, it does.
6.2.1.1.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where bodily formation does not arise, there does verbal formation not arise?
In the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, bodily formation does not arise there, but verbal formation does not fail to arise there.
In the fourth jhāna and among non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor verbal formation arises there.
Or, where verbal formation does not arise, there bodily formation does not arise?
In the second jhāna and the third jhāna, verbal formation does not arise there, but bodily formation does not fail to arise there.
In the fourth jhāna and among non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation arises there.
Where bodily formation does not arise, there does mental formation not arise?
In the fourth jhāna, in the fine-material sphere, and in the immaterial sphere, bodily formation does not arise there, but mental formation does not fail to arise there.
In non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor mental formation arises.
Or again, where ... [as before] ...? Yes.
Where verbal formation does not arise, there mental formation does not arise?
In the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna, there verbal formation does not arise; but it is not the case that there [mental formation does not arise].
The mental formation does not arise. Among non-percipient beings, there neither arises the verbal formation nor does the mental formation arise.
Or, where [neither arises]...? Yes. 6.2.1.1.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa).
For whom and where bodily formation does not arise, for them and there does verbal formation not arise?

At the moment of the arising of applied and sustained thought (vitakka-vicāra) without inhalation and exhalation, bodily formation does not arise for them there, but verbal formation does not fail to arise for them there.
[This is so] for all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, when there is no inhalation or exhalation.
At the moment of arising of a consciousness without applied thought and without sustained thought, and for non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor verbal formation arises therein.
Or, for whom and wherein...? Yes, they do.

(That which pertains to both [the person] and [the state] should be expanded in the same way as that which pertains to both [the person] and the state; however, in the section on "that which pertains to both," the phrase "those who have attained cessation" is not applicable.
Positive Person.
For whom bodily formation had arisen, for that person had verbal formation arisen? Yes.
Or conversely … pe … ? Yes.
For whom bodily formation had arisen, for that person had mental formation arisen? Yes.
Or for whomsoever... [as before] ...? Yes.
For whomsoever verbal formation had arisen, had mental formation arisen for him? Yes.
Or for whomsoever... [as before] ...? Yes.
6.2.1.2.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) had arisen … [etc.
… (The "where" section is identical in all respects.)
6.2.1.2.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what place, did bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arise;
in that same person, and in that same place, did verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arise?
In those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, bodily formation arose there, but [verbal formation did not].
And for those who had entered the first jhāna, both bodily formation and verbal formation arose there.
Or else, for whomsoever verbal formation had arisen in a certain place, had bodily formation also arisen for them in that same place?
For those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, verbal formation had arisen there,
but bodily formation had not arisen for them there. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those belonging to the sense-sphere,
both verbal formation and bodily formation had arisen there.
For whomsoever bodily formation had arisen at a certain place, for that person had mental formation arisen there? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation had arisen at a certain place, for that person had bodily formation arisen there?
For those who have attained the fourth jhāna, and for those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, mental formation had arisen there, but bodily formation had not.

There was the arising of mental formation for them there, but bodily formation did not arise for them there. For those who have attained the first jhāna, the second jhāna, or the third jhāna, and for those belonging to the sense-sphere realm,
both mental formation and bodily formation arose for them there.
For whomsoever verbal formation had arisen at a certain place, for that person had mental formation also arisen at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation had arisen at a certain place, for that person had verbal formation also arisen at that same place?
For those who have attained the second jhāna, the third jhāna, or the fourth jhāna, and for the inhabitants of the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) at the moment of their second consciousness.
While they were present there, mental formation arose for them, but vocal formation did not arise for them.
For those who have attained the first jhāna, for those of the sense-sphere realm, and for others of the fine-material and immaterial realms,
both mental formation and vocal formation arose there.
6.2.1.2.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom bodily formation had not arisen, for that person had verbal formation not arisen? None.
Or else, for whom verbal formation had not arisen, for that person had bodily formation not arisen? None.
For whom bodily formation had not arisen, for that person had mental formation not arisen? None.
Or again, for whom... [etc. ...none.
For whom verbal formation had not arisen, for that person had mental formation not arisen? None.
Or for whom... [etc.]? There is none.
6.2.1.2.5. Negative Plane: Where bodily formation did not arise... [etc.]...

In that case, verbal formation had not arisen. For those who have attained the fourth jhāna and for the Suddhāvāsa deities when their second moment of consciousness is occurring, and for non-percipient beings—verbal formation had not arisen and bodily formation had also not arisen there.
Or, conversely, where verbal formation had not arisen for someone, had bodily formation also not arisen for them there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, verbal formation did not arise therein;

yet bodily formation did not fail to arise for them there. For those who have attained the fourth jhāna, for the Suddhāvāsa deities while their second consciousness is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation arose therein.
For whom, where bodily formation had not arisen, for them there mental formation had not arisen?

For those who have attained the fourth jhāna, and for those in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—bodily formation had not arisen for them there, but it is not that mental formation had not arisen for them there. [It was not so] for those being reborn in the Pure Abodes.
For non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor mental formation had arisen there.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever... [etc.]? Yes.
For whomsoever and wherever vocal formation had not arisen, had mental formation not arisen for him there? Yes.

For those who have attained the second jhāna, the third jhāna, or the fourth jhāna, and for the Suddhāvāsa deities while their second moment of consciousness is occurring, verbal formation has not arisen therein, but mental formation has not failed to arise therein.
For those being reborn in the Suddhāvāsa realm and for non-percipient beings, verbal formation has not arisen therein... [and so on].
And mental formation did not arise.
Or for whom, and where...? Yes. 6.2.1.3.
Future Section.
6.2.1.3.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) will arise, for that person will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arise? Yes.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation will arise, for that person will bodily formation arise?
For that consciousness immediately after which the final consciousness of the sense-sphere will arise—
for those at the moment of death who are final-existence beings in the fine-material or immaterial spheres, and for those who, having been reborn in the fine-material or immaterial spheres,
will attain final nibbāna there— the verbal formation will arise, but the bodily formation will not arise for them.
In other cases, both verbal formation and bodily formation will arise.
For whom bodily formation will arise, will mental formation also arise for them? Yes.
Or rather, for whom mental formation will arise, will bodily formation also arise for them?
For those whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to the final consciousness of the sense-sphere,

for those final-existence beings in the fine-material or immaterial spheres, and for those who, having been reborn in the fine-material or immaterial spheres, will attain final Nibbāna at the moment of death—
for these, the mental formation will arise, but the bodily formation will not arise.
In others among them, both the mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will arise and the bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) will arise.
For whom verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) will arise, for that person will mental formation arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom mental formation will arise, for that person will verbal formation arise?
For those whose final consciousness will arise immediately after a state of consciousness that is without applied thought and sustained thought,
mental formation will arise for them, but verbal formation will not arise for them.
For others, both mental formation and verbal formation will arise.
6.2.1.3.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where bodily formation will arise … [etc.
… 6.2.1.3.3. Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whomsoever bodily formation will arise there, for that person will vocal formation arise there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, bodily formation will arise there, but vocal formation will not arise there for them.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those belonging to the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara), [both will arise].
In those persons, both bodily formation and verbal formation will arise there.
Or rather, for whomsoever verbal formation will arise in a certain place, will bodily formation also arise for that person in that same place? [Answer:

For one whose final consciousness of the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara) is about to arise immediately after a given state of consciousness, or for one whose [final consciousness] of the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) or immaterial sphere (arūpāvacara) [is about to arise].
For them, verbal formation will arise there, but bodily formation will not arise there for them.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for others belonging to the sense sphere,
both verbal formation and bodily formation will arise there.
For whomsoever bodily formation will arise in a certain place, for that person will mental formation arise there? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever mental formation will arise in a certain place, for that person will bodily formation arise there?
For one whose consciousness immediately precedes the final consciousness of the sense-sphere realm, or the fourth jhāna...
For those who have attained the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere, mental formation will arise there,
but bodily formation will not arise there for them. For those who have attained the first jhāna, the second jhāna, or the third jhāna,
as well as for others in the sense-sphere realm, both mental formation and bodily formation will arise there.
If verbal formation will arise for someone in a certain place, will mental formation also arise for that person in that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, if mental formation will arise for someone in a certain place, will verbal formation also arise for that person in that same place? [It will not.

For one whose final consciousness—immediately following which a subsequent consciousness without applied thought or sustained thought (avitakka-avicāra) will arise—is about to arise, or for one in the second jhāna...
For those who have attained the third jhāna or the fourth jhāna, mental formation will arise there,
but vocal formation will not arise for them there. For those who have attained the first jhāna, for those of the sense-sphere realm,
and for others of the fine-material and immaterial realms, both mental formation and [vocal formation] will arise there.
And verbal formation will arise.
6.2.1.3.4. Negative Person:
For whom bodily formation will not arise, for that person will verbal formation not arise?
For those whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to the final consciousness of the sense-sphere,

for those final-existence beings in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere, and for those who, having been reborn in the fine-material or immaterial sphere, will attain final Nibbāna at the moment of death—
for these, bodily formation will not arise, but it is not the case that vocal formation will not arise for them.

For those possessing the final consciousness, and for those whose final consciousness—which is without applied thought and sustained thought—will arise immediately after this consciousness, neither bodily formation nor verbal formation will arise.
Or, for whom...? Yes, they will not.
For whom bodily formation will not arise, for that person will mental formation not arise?
For one after whose consciousness the final consciousness of the sense-sphere arises;

for those final-existence beings in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere who, having been reborn in the fine-material or immaterial sphere, will attain final Nibbāna; and for those [others]—for them [bodily formation will not arise, and likewise mental formation will not arise].
For those who are passing away, bodily formation will not arise, but mental formation will not fail to arise for them.
For those possessing their final consciousness, neither bodily formation nor mental formation will arise.
Or, for whom mental formation [will not arise]...? Yes, it will.
For whom verbal formation will not arise, for them mental formation will not arise?

For those whose final consciousness—immediately following which a consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought will arise—verbal formation will not arise, but mental formation will not fail to arise for them. [This is so] for those possessing the final consciousness.
Verbal formation will not arise and mental formation will also not arise.
Or, for whom...? Yes. 6.2.1.3.5.
Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where bodily formation will not arise … [etc. … 6.2.1.3.6.
Negative Person-Location (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa):
For whom, where bodily formation will not arise, for that person there, will vocal formation not arise?

For those whose final consciousness of the sense sphere will arise immediately after this consciousness—namely, for those [consciousnesses] of the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—the bodily formation will not arise therein;
yet it is not the case that the verbal formation will not arise for them therein.
[This applies to] those possessing the final consciousness, and for whom a final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought will arise immediately after this consciousness.
For those who have attained the fourth jhāna and for non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor verbal formation will arise there. Or, conversely,
for whomsoever verbal formation will not arise in a certain place, will bodily formation also not arise for them there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna and the third jhāna, verbal formation will not arise there,
but bodily formation will not fail to arise for them there. [This is so] for one possessing the final consciousness, for one whose final consciousness—
immediately after which a final consciousness without initial application and sustained application will arise— and for those who have attained the fourth jhāna.
For non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation will arise there.
For whomsoever bodily formation will not arise in a certain place, will mental formation also not arise for them there?
[Yes. For that consciousness immediately after which the final consciousness of the sense-sphere realms will arise, or the fourth jhāna...
For those who have attained [jhāna] of the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere, bodily formation will not arise there,
but mental formation will not fail to arise for them there. For those possessing their final consciousness and for non-percipient beings,
neither bodily formation nor mental formation will arise there.
Or for whom, at whatever [place]...? Yes.
For whom, at whatever [place], verbal formation will not arise, for that person, at that place, will mental formation not arise?
For one whose final consciousness—following immediately after which a consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought (avitakka-avicāra) will arise—is the second jhāna.
For those who have attained the third jhāna or the fourth jhāna, verbal formation will not arise there,
but mental formation will not fail to arise for them there. For those possessing their final consciousness and for non-percipient beings,
neither verbal formation nor mental formation will arise there.
Or for whom, at whatever [place] …pe…? Yes.
6.2.1.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past. 6.2.1.4.1.
Positive Person.
For whom bodily formation arises, for that person did verbal formation arise? Yes.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation had arisen, for that person does bodily formation arise?

[It does not] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those who have entered cessation attainment.
In the case of non-percipient beings, verbal formation had arisen, but bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation had arisen and bodily formation also arises for them.
For whom bodily formation arises, has mental formation arisen for them? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever mental formation had arisen, does bodily formation arise for them?
For all those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation,
and for those who have entered the attainment of cessation or are non-percipient beings— mental formation had arisen for them, but bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, both mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) and bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) have arisen.
For one in whom verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arises, has mental formation arisen? Yes.
Or rather, for one in whom mental formation has arisen, does verbal formation arise?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought,
and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, mental formation has arisen, but verbal formation does not arise.
At the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought, both mental formation and verbal formation have arisen for them.
6.2.1.4.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where bodily formation arises … [etc.
… 6.2.1.4.3. Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whomsoever bodily formation arises there, for that person had verbal formation arisen there?

For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, bodily formation arises there, but verbal formation had not arisen there for them. [In the case of] the first jhāna...
In those who have attained [jhāna] and in those of the sense-sphere at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation,
both bodily formation and verbal formation arise there. Or conversely,
for whomsoever and wherever verbal formation has arisen, does bodily formation arise there for them?
At the moment of dissolution of inhalation and exhalation for those who have attained the first jhāna belonging to the sense sphere;

at the moment of arising of consciousness for those same persons when there is no inhalation or exhalation; and for those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—at these times, verbal formation has arisen for them there, but bodily formation does not arise for them there. (Regarding) the first jhāna...

In those who have entered the attainment [of the first jhāna], at the moment of the arising of the in-breaths and out-breaths of the sense-sphere, verbal formation has arisen and bodily formation arises there.
For whomsoever bodily formation arises in a certain place, has mental formation arisen for them there? Yes.
Or rather: for whomsoever, wherever mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) had arisen, does bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arise there for them?

For all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness when breath-in and breath-out are absent—mental formation had arisen for them there, but bodily formation does not arise for them there. [This is so] regarding breath-in and breath-out.
At the moment of arising, for those [beings], both mental formation and bodily formation had arisen there.
For whomsoever vocal formation arises there, had mental formation arisen there for that person? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation had arisen there, does vocal formation arise there for that person?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and in those without applied thought and sustained thought at the moment of the arising of consciousness,

mental formation has arisen there, but vocal formation does not arise there for them. In those at the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought, both mental formation and vocal formation have arisen there.
6.2.1.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom bodily formation does not arise, for that person did vocal formation not arise? It did arise.
Or else, for whom vocal formation did not arise, for that person does bodily formation not arise? There is none.
For whom bodily formation does not arise, for that person had mental formation not arisen? It had arisen.
Or rather, for whom mental formation had not arisen, for that person does bodily formation not arise? There is no such case.
For whom verbal formation does not arise, for that person had mental formation not arisen? It had arisen.
Or for whom... [etc. ...? There is none.
6.2.1.4.5. Negative Plane:
Where bodily formation does not arise... [etc. ...

6.2.1.4.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom, in what [sphere], does bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) not arise; for that same person, in that same [sphere], had verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) not already arisen? [Answer:
For those who have attained the first jhāna, and for those of the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara) at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation—for these very persons...

At the moment of arising of consciousness, in those [beings] without inhalation and exhalation—namely, those in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—the bodily formation does not arise therein;
yet, for them, the verbal formation has not failed to have arisen there.

This is also the case for those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, as well as for those very same persons without inhalation and exhalation.

At the moment of arising of consciousness in those who have attained the fourth jhāna, in the second moment of consciousness of those born in the Suddhāvāsa heavens, and in the case of non-percipient beings—among these, neither bodily formation nor verbal formation arises there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever verbal formation has not arisen at a certain place, does bodily formation not arise for them there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation,
verbal formation has not arisen therein, yet bodily formation does not fail to arise therein. For those very same persons,
at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation while having attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, [this is so] even without inhalation and exhalation.
At the moment of arising of consciousness in those who have attained the fourth jhāna, in the second moment of consciousness of the Suddhāvāsa deities,
and in non-percipient beings— therein, for them, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation has arisen.
For whomsoever, wherever, bodily formation does not arise, for that person, there, has mental formation not arisen?
In all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, and in those without breath-in and breath-out at the moment of the arising of consciousness,
bodily formation does not arise there, yet mental formation has not failed to arise there for them.
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes and for non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor mental formation has arisen there.
Or again, for whomsoever mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) had not arisen at a certain place, does bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) not arise for him there? Yes.
For whomsoever vocal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) does not arise at a certain place, had mental formation not arisen for him there?

[It has] for all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness when it is devoid of applied thought and sustained thought (vitakka-vicāra). At that place...
Verbal formation does not arise for them there, but mental formation has not failed to arise for them there either.
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), neither verbal formation nor mental formation has arisen there.
Or, for whom and where...? Yes, it is so.
6.2.1.5. Chapter on the Present and Future (Paccuppannānāgatavāra) 6.2.1.5.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arises, will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arise for that person? Yes.
Or again, for whomsoever verbal formation will arise, does bodily formation arise for that person?
For all those at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— verbal formation will arise for them, but bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation, both verbal formation (vacī-saṅkhāra) will arise and bodily formation (kāya-saṅkhāra) arises.
For whom bodily formation arises, will mental formation (citta-saṅkhāra) arise for that person? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom mental formation will arise, does bodily formation arise for that person?
In all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, in those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the arising of consciousness,
and in those who have attained the attainment of cessation or are non-percipient beings, mental formation will arise, but bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, for them both mental formation and bodily formation will arise.
For whom verbal formation arises, will mental formation arise for them?
At the moment of arising of the final consciousness accompanied by initial application and sustained application, verbal formation arises for them, but mental formation will not arise for them.
For others, at the moment of arising of initial application and sustained application, verbal formation [arises].
Does mental formation arise for that person, and will verbal formation also arise? Or, conversely, for whomsoever verbal formation will arise, does mental formation arise for that person?

[It does not] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, nor for those without initial application and sustained application at the moment of the arising of consciousness, nor for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, mental formation will arise, but verbal formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought, for those [beings], both mental formation and verbal formation will arise.
6.2.1.5.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Where bodily formation arises … [as above] … 6.2.1.5.3. Positive Person-Space:
For whom, where bodily formation arises, will verbal formation arise for that person there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation,

bodily formation arises there, but vocal formation will not arise for them there. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for sense-sphere beings at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, bodily formation [arises] there...
And does verbal formation arise [there]? Or, conversely, for whomsoever verbal formation will arise in a certain place, does bodily formation arise for them there?
For those who have attained the first jhāna, and for those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation—for them [it is so].
At the moment of arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation, for those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere,

verbal formation will arise there, but bodily formation does not arise for them there. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those of the sense-sphere at the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation [arises] there.
And the bodily formation will arise and the bodily formation is arising.
For whomsoever, wherever the bodily formation is arising, for that person there, will the mental formation arise? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever, wherever the mental formation will arise, for that person there, is the bodily formation arising?
In all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, and in those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the arising of consciousness,

mental formation will arise there, but bodily formation does not arise for them there. At the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, both mental formation and bodily formation will arise for them there.
For whom and where verbal formation arises, for that person and in that place will mental formation arise?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness accompanied by initial application and sustained application, verbal formation arises for them there, but mental formation will not arise for them there. [This is] at the moment of arising of initial application and sustained application in others.
In those [beings], both verbal formation arises there and mental formation will arise there.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever mental formation will arise there, does verbal formation arise there for them?

For all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness when it is devoid of initial application and sustained application, [verbal formation does not arise] there.

The mental formation will arise for them, but the verbal formation does not arise for them there. At the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought, both the mental formation and the verbal formation arise for them there.
6.2.1.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom bodily formation does not arise, for that person will verbal formation not arise?
For all those at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation,

and for those who have attained the attainment of cessation or are non-percipient beings— bodily formation does not arise for them, yet it is not the case that verbal formation will not arise for them.

For those possessing the final consciousness, and for those whose final consciousness—which is without applied thought and sustained thought—will arise immediately after this consciousness, neither the bodily formation nor the verbal formation arises.
Or rather, for whomsoever the verbal formation will not arise, does the bodily formation not arise for them? Yes, it does.
For whom bodily formation does not arise, for that person will mental formation not arise?
For all beings at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation,

and for those who have entered the attainment of cessation or are non-percipient beings— bodily formation does not arise for them, yet it is not the case that mental formation will not arise for them.
For those possessing the final consciousness, neither the bodily formation arises nor will the mental formation arise.
Or for whomsoever... [etc.]? Yes.
For whomsoever the verbal formation does not arise, will the mental formation not arise for him? Yes.

In all beings at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, in those who have attained cessation, and in non-percipient beings, verbal formation does not arise; yet it is not the case that mental formation will not arise for them.

[This is also the case] at the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by applied and sustained thought, and for those possessing the final consciousness without applied or sustained thought.
For them, neither vocal formation arises nor will mental formation arise.
Or, for whomsoever mental formation will not arise, does vocal formation not arise for them?
At the moment of the arising of the final consciousness accompanied by initial and sustained application, for them mental formation will not arise.

And yet, verbal formation does not fail to arise for them. At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by initial application and sustained application, and for those possessing the final consciousness without initial application and sustained application, neither mental formation nor verbal formation will arise, and verbal formation does not arise.
6.2.1.5.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where bodily formation does not arise … [etc. … 6.2.1.5.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa):
For whom, where bodily formation does not arise, will verbal formation not arise for that person there?
For those who have attained the first jhāna, at the moment of the dissolution of in-breaths and out-breaths belonging to the sense sphere;

for those same persons at the moment of the arising of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths; and for those of the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—at these times, bodily formation does not arise therein, yet it is not the case that verbal formation will not arise therein for them. [This is so] for those possessing their final consciousness.

For one whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to a final consciousness that is without applied thought and sustained thought—namely, for those who have attained the second or third jhāna at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation; for those same persons at the moment of the arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation;
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for non-percipient beings—in these cases, the bodily formation exists there.
And [it is such that] bodily formation does not arise and vocal formation will not arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever and wherever vocal formation will not arise, for that person there, does bodily formation not arise?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, for them there—
Verbal formation will not arise, yet bodily formation does not fail to arise for them there. This is the case for those possessing their final consciousness,
for those whose next consciousness after this one will be a final consciousness without initial application and sustained application,
for those who have attained the second or third jhāna, and at the moment of dissolution of inhalation and exhalation for those very persons when they are without inhalation and exhalation.
In the case of those who have attained the fourth jhāna at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and in the case of non-percipient beings,
neither verbal formation nor bodily formation arises there.
For whomsoever bodily formation does not arise in a certain place, will mental formation also not arise for them in that same place?
In all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, and in those without breath-in and breath-out at the moment of the arising of consciousness, bodily formation does not arise there;

yet, mental formation will not fail to arise for them there. For those possessing their final consciousness and for non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor mental formation arises there, nor will they arise.
Or rather: For whomsoever, wherever the mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will not arise, for that person there the bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) does not arise? Yes, it is so.
For whomsoever, wherever the verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) does not arise, for that person there the mental formation will not arise?

[It is so] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness without initial application and sustained application (vitakka-vicāra). Therein...

Verbal formation does not arise, yet mental formation will not fail to arise for them there. At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by initial and sustained application,
and for those possessing the final consciousness without initial or sustained application, as well as for non-percipient beings—
verbal formation does not arise and mental formation will also not arise for them there.
Or, for whomsoever mental formation will not arise at a certain place, will verbal formation not arise for them there?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, mental formation will not arise for them there, but verbal formation does not fail to arise for them there. At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought...

For those possessing the final consciousness that is without initial application and sustained application, and for non-percipient beings, neither the mental formation nor the verbal formation will arise, and the verbal formation does not arise there.
6.2.1.6. Chapter on the Past and Future.
6.2.1.6.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) has arisen, will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arise for that person?

For those possessing their final consciousness, and for one whose final consciousness—free from initial application and sustained application (avitakka-avicāra)—will arise immediately after the present consciousness.
In those persons, bodily formation had arisen, but vocal formation will not arise.
In other persons, both bodily formation had arisen and vocal formation will arise.
Or, for whomsoever...? Yes.
For whom bodily formation had arisen, will mental formation arise for them?
For those possessing the final consciousness, bodily formation had arisen, but mental formation will not arise for them. For others, both bodily formation had arisen and mental formation will arise.
Or rather, for whom... [etc. Yes.
For whom verbal formation has arisen, will mental formation arise for that person?

For those possessing their final consciousness, verbal formation has arisen, but mental formation will not arise for them. For others, both verbal formation has arisen and mental formation will arise.
Or, for whom... [etc.]? Yes.
6.2.1.6.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) had arisen … [etc.
… 6.2.1.6.3. Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whomsoever bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) had arisen at a certain place, will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arise for them at that same place?

For those possessing their final consciousness in the sense-sphere realm (kāmāvacara), and for those who have attained the second or third jhāna, bodily formation had arisen there, but verbal formation will not arise for them there. [However, this is not the case] for those in the first jhāna...
For those who have attained [jhāna] and for others belonging to the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara), both bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) has arisen and verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) will arise therein.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever verbal formation will arise therein, has bodily formation arisen therein for them?
For those belonging to the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) and the immaterial sphere (arūpāvacara), verbal formation will arise therein, but bodily formation has not [arisen] for them.
In that case, bodily formation had arisen. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those of the sense-sphere realm, both verbal formation will arise and bodily formation had arisen there.
For whomsoever bodily formation had arisen in a certain place, will mental formation also arise for them in that same place?
For those in the sense-sphere who possess their final consciousness, bodily formation has arisen there,
but mental formation will not arise there for them. For those who have attained the first jhāna, the second jhāna, or the third jhāna, as well as for others in the sense-sphere,
both bodily formation and mental formation have arisen there and will also arise there.
Or, for whomsoever mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will arise at a certain place, has bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arisen for them there?

For those who have attained the fourth jhāna, and for those belonging to the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) and the immaterial sphere (arūpāvacara), mental formation will arise there, but bodily formation has not arisen for them there. [This is so] for those who have attained the first jhāna and the second jhāna...
For those who have attained the third jhāna and for those of the sense-sphere realm,
mental formation will arise there and bodily formation has arisen there.
For whomsoever verbal formation has arisen in a certain place, will mental formation arise for that person in that same place?
In those who possess the final consciousness on the plane of initial application and sustained application, verbal formation has arisen there,
but mental formation will not arise there for them. In others on the plane of initial application and sustained application,
both verbal formation and mental formation have arisen and will arise there.
Or rather, for whomsoever mental formation will arise at a certain plane, will verbal formation have arisen for them at that same plane?
For those on a plane without initial application and without sustained application (*avitakka-avicāra-bhūmi*), mental formation will arise there, but verbal formation has not arisen for them there.
For those on a plane with initial application and sustained application (*savitakka-savicāra-bhūmi*), both mental formation and...
There will arise a verbal formation, and a bodily formation has arisen.
6.2.1.6.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala):
For whom a bodily formation has not arisen, will a verbal formation not arise for them? None.
Or, for whom verbal formation will not arise, had bodily formation not arisen for him? It had arisen.
For whom bodily formation had not arisen, will mental formation not arise for him? There is none.
Or, for whom mental formation will not arise, had bodily formation not arisen for him? It had arisen.
For whom verbal formation had not arisen, for that person will mental formation not arise? None.
Or rather, for whom mental formation will not arise, for that person had verbal formation not arisen? It had arisen.
6.2.1.6.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where bodily formation had not arisen … [etc] … 6.2.1.6.6.
Negative Person-Space: For whom, where bodily formation had not arisen, will verbal formation not arise there?
For those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, bodily formation had not arisen there,
yet vocal formation will not fail to arise for them there. [This is the case] for those in the fine-material and immaterial spheres who possess their final consciousness,
for whom the final consciousness— free from applied thought and sustained thought— will arise immediately after that [preceding] consciousness, and for those in the fourth jhāna.
For those who have attained the attainment of non-percipient beings, there neither arose bodily formation nor will vocal formation arise therein.
Or else, for whomsoever vocal formation will not arise therein, had bodily formation not arisen therein for them?
For those in the sense-sphere who possess their final consciousness, and for those who have attained the second or third jhāna—[for them...]
In that case, verbal formation will not arise, but bodily formation has not failed to arise for them there.

[This is true] for those possessing the final consciousness in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere; for those whose final consciousness—immediately after which a consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought will arise;
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for non-percipient beings—in these cases, for them there, [verbal formation will not arise].
And verbal formation will not arise, and bodily formation has not arisen.
For whomsoever, wherever, bodily formation has not arisen, will mental formation not arise for them there?
For those who have attained the fourth jhāna, and for those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—for them, there, bodily formation...
It has not arisen for them there, yet mental formation will not fail to arise for them there. For those possessing their final consciousness in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere,
and for non-percipient beings, both bodily formation and mental formation have not arisen and will not arise there.
Or, for whomsoever mental formation will not arise at a certain place, has bodily formation not arisen for them there?
For those possessing their final consciousness in the sense-sphere realm, mental formation will not arise there, but bodily formation had not failed to arise for them there.
[The same applies] for those possessing their final consciousness in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere.
For non-percipient beings, neither the mental formation nor the bodily formation will arise there.
For one in whom the verbal formation has not arisen at a certain place, will the mental formation not arise for them at that same place?
For those on a plane devoid of both initial and sustained application of mind, the verbal formation has not arisen there; yet for them, [the mental formation] does not [necessarily] not arise there.

Will mental formation not arise? For those possessing their final consciousness on a plane without initial application and sustained application, and for non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor mental formation has arisen there, nor will mental formation arise there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation will not arise in a certain place, has verbal formation not arisen there for them?
For those possessing the final consciousness on the plane of with-applied-thought and with-sustained-thought, mental formation will not arise there,
but verbal formation had not failed to arise for them there. For those possessing the final consciousness on the plane of without-applied-thought and without-sustained-thought,
and for non-percipient beings, neither mental formation nor verbal formation will arise there, nor had they arisen there.
The Section on Arising.
